How do you stay warm in a winter power outage?

Scenarios Updated 2026-08-08

Heat the person rather than the room. On the largest machine in this library that states enough about itself to be divided, a heated blanket runs for 23 h and a 1,500 W space heater for 1.1 h — the same battery, about 22× the warmth in time. All 12 published US machines here carry the blanket; only 5 pass the heater outright.

One caveat belongs in the first paragraph rather than a footnote. The only citable wattage for a heated blanket in this library is a European manual’s, because US makers print theirs on the product’s own label instead of in any document; the engine falls through to that figure for US pairings, and every blanket hour above rests on it.

This is the clearest case on the site of a question that no ranked list of power stations can answer. Every machine in the library passes the blanket, so ranking them against it separates nothing; 12 of 12 rows are the same verdict. The decision that actually changes the outcome is which appliance you plug in, and that decision costs a fraction of what the next battery size up costs.

Why the blanket figure is European, stated plainly

The US half of this record carries a dated absence block rather than a number. Two US heated-bedding manuals were re-read for a wattage on 2026-08-07: both state the supply — a 110–120 V outlet in one, a standard 120 V outlet at 60 Hz in the other — and both document the automatic shut-off, and neither carries a technical data table of the kind the European maker prints, so we found no published US wattage in either. The record’s own note expects that figure to live on the product’s physical rating label, and a label stitched into a blanket is not a document we can cite. So the engine resolves the US region to the record’s top-level figure, which is the European one. The quantity at stake is tens of watts against a load that every machine here clears by a wide margin, and the ratio this article turns on survives it — but the substitution is real and it belongs on the page rather than in a footnote.

The appliance stops before the battery does

Both US manuals on this record document the same safety behaviour: the controller switches itself off after 10 h of continuous use, and after 3 h for a throw. A machine that would carry the blanket for 23 h will meet that timer twice before it runs low. It is an unusual shape for an outage answer and a welcome one: the limit is a switch you can press rather than a battery you have to buy.

What this library cannot model

Anything that burns fuel. Every figure on this site is electrical, and we do not publish numbers for combustion heaters of any kind, indoors or out. The one fuel-burning load in the library is an air heater for a vehicle, and what our record holds for it is the electricity its fan and glow plug use, not the heat it makes. The other thing worth saying about cold: the battery itself is affected by it, and a machine kept in an unheated garage will not deliver what its record says.

Questions people ask

How many watts does an electric blanket use?
A European maker’s technical data table states 55–65 W for a single and 85–100 W for a double, on a 220–240 V supply. There is no equivalent figure for a US model in this library: two US heated-bedding manuals were re-read on 2026-08-07 and both state the outlet voltage and the automatic shut-off without a technical data table, so we found no published US wattage in either. Our engine falls through to the European figure for US pairings.
How long will a power station run a space heater?
About an hour on a 2,000 Wh class machine, and that is the whole battery. The record here is a 1,500 W resistive heater, and a heating element simply turns whatever it is given into heat, so there is nothing to shop for on efficiency: five of the twelve published US machines here pass it outright, three are downgraded and four refuse it. A heated blanket on the same machine runs for roughly a day.
How do you stay warm during a power outage without a generator?
Move the heat closer to the person. On one 2,000 Wh class battery, our engine computes about 23 hours for a heated blanket against 1.1 hours for a 1,500 W space heater — the same machine, about twenty times the duration, because one appliance warms a bed and the other tries to warm a room through the walls. If the house has gas heat, powering the furnace blower is the other efficient route, though this library will not issue a pass on that load.
